central_native.detail: Ed25519 9; hashes25; forced ECDSA reference18+native2; RSA4 valid/22 malformed plus99 imports; Secp22 normal and3 forced each in debug/release.

central_public.breakdown: 3 fixed-curve public fixtures +2 combined signature/prepared composition fixtures +8 nominal serialization/cross-plugin rejections

central_ash.confirmed_gc: MLDSA, MLDSAPrepared, HashLifecycle and PreparedComposition include explicit reclamation/lifetime assertions; correctness metrics are not performance comparisons.

production_review: Independent reviewer approved the production changes, failing-before/passing-after regressions and final Secp256k1 emitted Wasm.

commands.environment: From frozen SDK: nix develop --command bash <integration wrapper>; PATH starts with SDK/bin, MOTOKO_CORE is pinned Core2.5.0; build/test jobs2; one PocketIC runner.
commands.build: python3 scripts/build.py --motoko "$SDK" --skip-motoko-build base58 bech32 blake3 bls12-381 candidx cbor ed25519 hmac-sha2 json ml-dsa p256 ripemd160 rsa secp256k1 sha256 sha512
commands.native: python3 tests/build-config.py; cargo test --locked --jobs 2 --target-dir _build/native-tests; bash tests/crypto-audit/round5/<lane>/run-native.sh for each registered adapter
commands.public: test-runner -b -j2 packages/fast/tests/run/{crypto-p256,crypto-secp256k1,crypto-secp256k1-audit5}.mo tests/integration/run/{signature-composition,prepared-composition}.mo tests/integration/fail (absolute paths from SDK root)
commands.ash: bun "$ASH/src/index.ts" test packages/fast/tests/ash/<suite>.ash.json --verbose for each listed suite; frozen private Ash selects SDK/bin/moc
commands.benchmark: prepared/build.py with unchanged round4/secp256k1/cases.json and original baseline frozen case-root, current fast/dist, fixed SDK/RTS; prepared/run.mjs --trials 3; round4/compare.py --target-plugin secp256k1

limitations: Finite regression coverage and internal independent review; no external cryptographic certification, whole-program timing proof, secret-erasure guarantee, arbitrary invalid-pointer fuzzing or exact retained-heap claim. The forced rare cases inject only controlled test seams into temporary copies of production source.
